plan.estimand: Minimum total sample size for binary outcome prediction model development meeting Riley criteria: apparent versus adjusted R-squared shrinkage ≤0.05 (Nagelkerke scale) with 95% CI, targeting outcome-risk absolute margin of error 0.05
plan.hypothesis: Development sample is sufficient for logistic regression model with 10 candidate predictors to satisfy shrinkage and precision constraints under anticipated effect and validation conditions
assumptions: Logistic regression model for binary outcome prediction
10 candidate predictors to be evaluated and potentially retained
Outcome prevalence 0.20 in development sample
Anticipated adjusted Cox-Snell R-squared 0.12 post-development
Anticipated shrinkage factor 0.95 (5% expected shrinkage) on validation
Default Riley precision criteria: maximum absolute (apparent − adjusted) R-squared difference 0.05 on Nagelkerke scale with 95% confidence
Outcome-risk absolute margin of error target 0.05 for prediction precision
Model performance stability and calibration within specified precision bounds
scientific_notes: pmsampsize package 1.1.3 implements Riley et al. (2020) sample-size calculation for prediction model development
Binary outcome uses logistic regression; Cox-Snell R-squared is the development-sample apparent effect size
Shrinkage 0.95 means anticipated 5% reduction in model performance on independent validation (validated R-squared = 0.95 × 0.12)
Riley precision criteria control overfitting risk via constraints on apparent versus adjusted R-squared difference
Nagelkerke R-squared is scale-invariant and preferred for binary/survival outcomes
Outcome-risk precision (absolute margin of error 0.05) addresses predictive uncertainty for binary event probability estimates
User requests verification of outcome-risk precision at returned sample size
